title: Onboarding micro-bench harness refactor for deterministic model profiling
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Refactor the benchmark harness used during model onboarding to produce deterministic, per-model microbenchmarks and publish standardized performance profiles to the profile registry. This ticket covers dataset fingerprinting, deterministic prompt seeding, lightweight runner adapters for microbench kernels (short/med/long seq lengths), and an artifact format that includes pinned model version, quantization flags, hardware hints, and warmup metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run per-model microbench suites (3 sequence-length buckets) with the same seed producing identical token latencies across 3 consecutive runs on staging
Published profile JSON includes: model_version, quantization_profile, sequence_distribution, median_p50_p99_latency_ms, avg_tokens_per_second, kv_cache_warmup_steps, and sampling_seed
PRs for harness refactor merged and gated behind a feature flag (harness_microbench_refactor) with CI coverage in onboarding pipeline
Profile artifacts are uploaded to the profile registry and visible in the Console staging catalog with linkable artifact revision and verification checksum
End-to-end onboarding flow for a sample open model demonstrates pinned rollout to runtime-1.24 using the new profile without manual intervention
implementation_notes: Split existing large profile run into: microbench driver (fast, deterministic) + full eval runner (stochastic evals kept separate)
Introduce dataset fingerprinting: compute sha256 of canonicalized prompt set and store as dataset_id in profile metadata
Deterministic prompt seeding: replace current RNG with seeded PRNG (xoshiro256+) and persist sampling_seed in profiles
Runner adapters: add three kernel-targeted runners (tiny/short/long) that exercise typical WS and KV cache paths; each runner reports warmup behavior

Artifact schema v2: bump profile schema to include hardware_hint (e.g., a100-40gb, t4), quantize_flag, and kernel_tag; ensure backwards compatibility by publishing both v1 and v2 when running in staging
CI: add a smoke check that validates uploaded profile JSON against the schema and verifies checksum matches the artifact storage entry
Performance noise: run 3 sequential microbench repeats and record median; do not attempt heavy statistical tests in microbench suite (keep full eval harness for quality/regression detection)
progress_updates: 2026-03-06: Spike completed comparing PRNGs for deterministic sampling; xoshiro256+ chosen for speed and reproducibility across languages. Notes in GH gist: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/gists/seed-spike
2026-03-08: Prototype microbench runner implemented for 'short' seq-length using existing runtime hooks. Local runs show <2% variance after 3 repeats when run in isolation on staging-gpu-03

2026-03-10: Design review with PM & Console team — agreed to include dataset_id and sampling_seed in profile metadata and expose a 'verify artifact' flow in Console. Meeting notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONB/Microbench+Profile+Design

2026-03-12: Draft PR created: GH PR #1487 with harness refactor and new profile schema v2. Requesting eng review from @mariela and @kevin. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/pull/1487
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Microbench determinism may be impacted by background system noise on shared staging GPUs. Mitigation: run microbenches on isolated reserved slots and record system load; if noise > 5% mark profile as noisy and re-run in dedicated queue

Risk: Publishing v2 artifacts may break older consumers. Mitigation: dual-publish v1-compatible minimal profile along with v2 rich metadata for 2 release cycles and add runtime feature flag for v2 consumption

Risk: Dataset fingerprint collisions if canonicalization differs across languages. Mitigation: publish canonicalizer spec and include canonicalized text hash plus prompt-set size to reduce collision probability
